UK FCA Considers Regulatory Exemptions for Tokenized Gold The UK’s FCA is considering a bespoke regulatory regime for tokenized gold, including potential exemptions from collective investment scheme and alternative investment fund rules, the Financial Times reports. The FCA is working with the Treasury and the Bank of England on the proposal. No decisions have been made. The Bank of England is also considering whether tokenized assets, including stablecoins, could qualify as collateral under its Sterling Monetary Framework. — link

EU Cyber Resilience Act Takes Effect, Crypto Wallet Vulnerabilities Must Be Reported Within 24 Hours The EU’s Cyber Resilience Act now requires in-scope commercial hardware wallet and wallet software manufacturers to report actively exploited vulnerabilities or serious security incidents to cyber authorities within 24 hours, according to CryptoSlate. A full notification is due within 72 hours. Final vulnerability reports must be submitted within 14 days after corrective or mitigating measures become available, while final reports for serious incidents are due one month after the 72-hour notification. The reporting rules took effect on Sept. 11, 2026, while broader product-security obligations will begin on Dec. 11, 2027. — link

Brazil’s Strict Capital Rules Could Push Most Crypto Firms Out of the Market Brazil’s central bank now requires VASPs to meet stricter capital and compliance requirements, with some firms facing capital requirements of up to BRL 37.2 million (about $7.2 million). Of roughly 300 VASPs in Brazil, only 20–25 are estimated to qualify for licensing, with around 10 expected to ultimately be approved. VASPs must apply by Oct. 30. Those that do not apply will have 30 days to wind down operations. Bitnuvem, NovaDAX, Digitra and Coinext have announced plans to end or restructure their retail businesses, without explicitly citing the new rules. — link

Highlight Clip: Bybit CEO: Crypto Retail Participation May Have Fallen About 30% Bybit CEO: Crypto Retail Participation May Have Fallen About 30% On April 15, 2026, Bybit CEO Ben Zhou said in a Cointelegraph interview at Paris Blockchain Week that crypto retail participation may be about 30% below peak levels, calling it a normal part of the market cycle. He said the market is waiting for a new catalyst, with meme coins driving the last cycle and AI potentially driving this one. — link
